transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello doctor. I'm here because I've been feeling completely exhausted all the time, and I can't seem to stop constantly worrying. It's been going on like this for about two years and four months now, and I just feel so drained.
During these past two years, have you also felt down or depressed most days, or has the main problem been constant worry and feeling on edge?
The main issue has definitely been the constant worrying and feeling tense all the time. I don't really feel down or depressed, but I just feel constantly wound up and on edge.
Do you find that the worrying is hard to control, even when you try to relax or tell yourself to stop?
Yes, absolutely. Even when I consciously try to tell myself to stop or try to relax, the thoughts just keep rushing in. I feel completely powerless to shut them down or control them.
Along with the worry, have you also been having symptoms like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, feeling restless, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, or being more irritable?

Yes, I definitely experience several of those. My body constantly feels incredibly stiff and tense, and I feel so restless and keyed up that I just can't relax. I also get exhausted very easily, and my concentration is terrible because my mind often goes completely blank.
Has this worrying been causing significant problems in your daily life, like at work, in relationships, or with everyday responsibilities?

Yes, it has caused huge disruptions in my daily life, especially at work. I find it incredibly hard to focus on my tasks because my worries constantly surface and scatter my attention. On top of that, I feel such a profound loss of energy that even basic, everyday responsibilities feel completely overwhelming.
Have these symptoms seemed related to any medical condition, medications, caffeine or other substances, or do they happen independently of those?
No, I don't think they are related to any other medical conditions, medications, caffeine, or other substances. They just seem to happen completely on their own, independent of anything like that.
